newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand reassures investors on ailing bank shrs.
newsitem.headline: Thailand reassures investors on ailing bank shrs.

text.p: Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Friday that shareholders of ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc should not panic over the recent plunge in the bank's share price.
The bank's shares fell up to 12 baht on Thursday when it started trading again after an 11-month suspension. But on Friday it rose the 10 percent daily limit and was up 0.30 baht at four baht.
Rerngchai told reporters the central bank had asked the troubled bank to make a sizeable amount of provisions for doubful and bad loans as part of an overall plan to write off the bank's huge debts.
"The write-off of the bad loans will enable the bank to post a profit this year," he said.
Shares of troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce's fell by over 75 percent of their value on Thursday as investors offloaded stock on worries that the bank may be delisted by the bourse.
The Thai stock exchange had allowed trading in the bank's shares to resume for one month from April 17, after a 11-month suspension, to assess whether it needed to be delisted.
From May 19, the share would be suspended again.
The exchange said last week that the bank's deteriorating financial position made it a candidate for delisting.
The bank last week revised net losses for 1996 to a hefty 24.85 billion baht ($955.8 million) after the central bank instructed it to raise provisions for doubtful and non-performing loans.
Its 1996 results were revised from a previously announced unaudited 1996 net loss of 2.84 billion baht.

The government took over the ailing bank in May 1996 to save it from a massive run on its deposits after it was found saddled with big debts. The bank said it had been saddled with net non-performing loans, after collateral deduction, valued at 53.78 billion baht at end-1996.
The Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand Plc has been asked by the central bank to help manage the troubled bank and the institution has taken an 18 percent stake in the bank.

Rerngchai said IFCT nominees were expected to start runing the bank from May 1 after a bank shareholders meeting on April 30 approved a new management team and plans proposed by IFCT and central bank to rehabilitate the bank.
